title: Closure of bounded-width DNFs under disjunction
statement: Let $f_1, \dots, f_m$ be Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$, and let $\ell$ be a natural number. Suppose that each $f_i$ is computed by some DNF formula of width at most $\ell$, that is, a disjunction of terms in which every term has at most $\ell$ literals. Then their disjunction $x \mapsto f_1(x) \lor \cdots \lor f_m(x)$ is also computed by a single DNF formula of width at most $\ell$.
hypotheses_covered: a finite list of Boolean functions on n variables (the children)
each child is computed by some DNF of width at most l
replaced:
Dual to the AND case: if an OR gate has children each expressible by a DNF of width at
most $\ell$, then the OR of all children is computed by a single DNF of width at most
$\ell$, obtained by concatenating the children's term lists.
